work.title: Work
work.intro: Three projects in production. For each one: what you see, and the machine driving it.

pulpina.name: Pulpiña RD
pulpina.alt: Pulpiña RD home page with its three stores: Moon, Sunshine and Men
pulpina.summary: An alternative fashion store in the Dominican Republic, with three sub-brands sharing one catalog.
pulpina.problem: Pulpina ran its sales almost entirely through Instagram, handwritten notes, and memory — no centralized catalog, no reliable tracking, and no way to search products or analyze the business. Checking sales and preparing reports could take most of a workday.
pulpina.role: I designed and developed Pulpina's e-commerce platform and internal operations system: the storefront and the admin tools behind it. Unlike STEMise and Together Sports, I also continue to manage and maintain it myself.
pulpina.process: I mapped the existing workflow and rebuilt it around one centralized system: a customer-facing store plus admin tools for products, orders, inventory, and sales — built around their real first-come-first-served order process, not a generic e-commerce setup.
pulpina.results: Centralized a catalog of roughly 300-500 products, replacing Instagram. Added searchable products, order management, and inventory tools, and automated recurring sales work. The business now runs significantly easier, with more purchases since launch.
pulpina.impact: In September 2026 alone: 347 users (+91% vs. August), 498 sessions, 4,188 page views, 764 products viewed, and 133 add-to-carts (+565%).

stemise.name: STEMise
stemise.alt: STEMise home page with its headline, navigation and calls to action
stemise.summary: The platform for a youth-led STEM education nonprofit active in more than 30 countries.
stemise.problem: STEMise already had a website, but it wasn't doing what the organization needed. People couldn't easily donate, volunteer, partner with STEMise, or access its STEM kits and learning paths — and the organization lacked the digital systems to support those interactions.
stemise.role: I completely redesigned and rebuilt STEMise's digital presence from the ground up: branding, visual identity, UX, content, frontend, backend, CMS, and forms. Since launch, the STEMise team runs the site day to day — I built it to work without me.
stemise.process: Rather than redesigning the site page by page, I rebuilt the experience around how people interact with STEMise — learning about it, donating, volunteering, and partnering. I built the architecture and a CMS giving the team full control over changes.
stemise.results: Completely replaced the previous website and digital experience. Built a CMS for the site's content, added donation, volunteer, and partnership forms, and created a platform for STEM kits and learning paths. The site is live and actively used.
stemise.impact: $35K+ raised, 159K+ people reached, 2,000+ students empowered, 100+ members, 102 countries represented, and 200K+ impressions.

togethersport.name: Together Sports
togethersport.alt: Together Sports home page with its motto Play Loud. Build Strong. and program photos
togethersport.summary: A youth sports nonprofit running four programs under a single brand.
togethersport.problem: Together Sports existed entirely offline. There was no website, no digital brand, and no central place to understand the organization, discover its programs, or find class information — their only online presence was a USTA booking page for free classes.
togethersport.role: I built Together Sports' digital presence from zero: the logo, brand identity, visual system, website, database, CMS, blog, and the infrastructure behind it. As with STEMise, I handed it off after launch — the organization runs it on their own from here.
togethersport.process: I started with the brand and visual identity, then designed the site around how people interact with Together Sports — program info, story, impact, blog content, and class availability, all in one hub, connected live to their USTA data.
togethersport.results: Created Together Sports' first complete digital presence and established its visual identity and brand system. Built a custom website, database, CMS, and blog, integrating live USTA class data. The site is now active in the organization's growth.
togethersport.impact: 2,000+ youth coached, 20 communities served, 3,300+ volunteer hours, 40 coaches trained, 10 partner organizations, and 1,500+ pieces of equipment donated.
